queue.name: Brent NHS Talking Therapies
queue.reason: The NHS page publishes this as the service telephone and states patients can self-refer by phone.
queue.evidence: The referral and contact sections both list the same service number.

queue.name: Brent Works — jobs and employment support
queue.reason: The Brent Works portal publishes this direct contact number.
queue.evidence: The portal footer lists the Brent Civic Centre contact telephone.

queue.name: Camden Adult Social Care
queue.currentValue: Use the online contact form or call and say “Adult Social Care”.
queue.proposedValue: Complete the online form for yourself or someone else. If you have difficulty with the form, need urgent support or are concerned about immediate safety, call and say “Adult Social Care”.
queue.reason: The council specifies when to use the telephone route rather than listing it as a general alternative.
queue.evidence: The council directs requests to the online form and gives the contact number for form difficulties, urgent needs or immediate safety concerns.

queue.name: Camden drug and alcohol service
queue.currentValue: Refer yourself or someone else online, or call to discuss support.
queue.proposedValue: You can refer yourself online or call to ask about support. Professionals referring someone else need that person’s permission.
queue.reason: The listing presents referring someone else as a general route. The provider identifies a separate professional form and explicitly requires consent.
queue.evidence: The service links separately to self-referral and professional referrals. The latter requires the referring professional to confirm the person has agreed to be contacted.

queue.name: Camden Job Hub and Disability Job Hub
queue.currentValue: Register through Good Work Camden and explain the support or adjustments you would like.
queue.proposedValue: Register with Good Work Camden or use the Job Hub email link to contact an adviser. For the Disability Job Hub, the council asks you to say you are disabled when you register.
queue.reason: The current instruction omits the disability declaration specifically requested for the specialist hub and the general email enquiry route.
queue.evidence: The council offers registration or email for general advice. For the Disability Job Hub, it asks residents to register and identify themselves as disabled on that registration.

queue.name: London Irish Centre: advice
queue.currentValue: Find the London Irish Centre contact route in Camden Advice Network.
queue.proposedValue: Ask the centre for an appointment by phone (choose option 1 twice) or use the email link on its advice page. If neither works for you, check its Camden Square reception hours.
queue.reason: The existing listing directs callers through a council directory instead of giving the direct booking route.
queue.evidence: The provider accepts booking enquiries by telephone or email. Its Camden Square reception is an alternative for people unable to use these routes.

queue.name: London Irish Centre: advice
queue.currentValue: Ask about appointments and which advice the centre can currently offer.
queue.proposedValue: Advice is by appointment. Check reception hours before visiting. The centre gives housing advice but does not find private accommodation.
queue.reason: The current wording asks visitors to check whether an appointment is needed; the provider says it is required.
queue.evidence: The service page requires booked appointments and distinguishes housing advice from finding private accommodation.

queue.name: London Irish Centre: advice
queue.currentValue: https://www.camden.gov.uk/camden-advice-network
queue.proposedValue: https://londonirishcentre.org/our-services/advice-information-support/
queue.reason: Link directly to the advice service and its booking information.
queue.evidence: The current council list links onward to the provider; the provider’s own advice page contains contact routes and service limitations.

queue.name: London Irish Centre: advice
queue.reason: Add the public booking number for people who cannot use online contact.
queue.evidence: The advice service publishes this number and asks callers to choose option 1 twice.

queue.name: Mary Ward Legal Centre
queue.currentValue: Call or use the relevant enquiry form to ask whether the centre can help.
queue.proposedValue: For housing, use the online form on Monday. If you cannot complete it, call Monday or Wednesday, 10am–noon; help filling it in is available on Monday only. For debt or benefits, use the separate contact instructions on the homepage.
queue.reason: The general access wording omits the one-day housing form and the phone alternative.
queue.evidence: Housing intake is online on Mondays. The provider gives two morning phone windows for people unable to use the form, but assisted form completion is only offered on Monday.

queue.name: Mary Ward Legal Centre
queue.currentValue: Ask about eligibility and capacity before travelling. The centre may not be able to take every case.
queue.proposedValue: Housing capacity is limited. If you get no reply within five days, seek another adviser. As of 21 November 2026, no pro bono appointments are available; check the homepage before trying to book.
queue.reason: The centre gives a specific reduced-capacity notice for housing and reports that pro bono appointments are unavailable.
queue.evidence: The homepage says to seek another housing adviser after five days without a response. Its hoped-for reopening of the pro bono form is not a confirmed appointment date.

queue.name: Mary Ward Legal Centre
queue.currentValue: People on a low income in London; case and funding criteria apply.
queue.proposedValue: Londoners on low incomes are the priority. For housing advice, people who live, work or study in Camden do not need to qualify for Legal Help. Eligibility differs by service.
queue.reason: The listing does not explain the local exception for housing enquiries.
queue.evidence: The housing team expressly exempts people who live, work or study in Camden from the Legal Help eligibility requirement for advice, while prioritising low income.

queue.name: Mind in Camden
queue.currentValue: Check joining arrangements. Mind in Camden says it does not offer a counselling or drop-in service.
queue.proposedValue: There is no drop-in service. Phoenix support groups are free. Separate one-to-one counselling costs £35 per weekly session after an assessment.
queue.reason: The listing rules out a counselling service that is now advertised.
queue.evidence: The dedicated counselling page describes individual sessions, assessment and the fee; the main page distinguishes free groups from drop-ins.

queue.name: Nafsiyat Intercultural Therapy Centre
queue.currentValue: Ask whether funded or paid therapy applies, and about assessment and waiting times.
queue.proposedValue: The short-term individual therapy programme is free for Camden residents. Ask about current availability; the centre also has a separate paid service.
queue.reason: The listing does not distinguish the free local programme from other services.
queue.evidence: The individual therapy page explicitly includes Camden, describes the sessions as free and signposts the separate paid service.

queue.name: Nafsiyat Intercultural Therapy Centre
queue.currentValue: Contact the centre to ask about referral and the languages and support available.
queue.proposedValue: Use the self-referral link on the individual therapy page, or contact the centre to ask about languages and availability. Health professionals have a referral route too.
queue.reason: The programme explicitly lists self-referral as well as professional referral.
queue.evidence: The programme page offers both routes and warns that therapists may be fully booked.

queue.name: New Horizon Youth Centre
queue.currentValue: https://www.camden.gov.uk/camden-advice-network
queue.proposedValue: https://nhyouthcentre.org.uk/young-person/get-help/
queue.reason: The listing sends people to a council directory instead of the provider’s access information.
queue.evidence: The Get Help page gives direct routes for young people.

queue.name: New Horizon Youth Centre
queue.currentValue: Use Camden Advice Network’s New Horizon listing to reach the centre and ask for help.
queue.proposedValue: If you are aged 16 to 24 and facing homelessness in London, you can come to the day centre in the morning or use the self-referral route on its Get Help page.
queue.reason: People can approach the provider directly.
queue.evidence: The provider describes its morning drop-in and invites young people at risk of homelessness to attend or self-refer.

queue.name: CNWL Recovery and Wellbeing College
queue.currentValue: https://www.cnwl.nhs.uk/services/recovery-and-wellbeing-college/how-enrol-recovery-and-wellbeing-college
queue.proposedValue: https://www.cnwl.nhs.uk/services/recovery-and-wellbeing-college/how-to-become-a-student
queue.reason: The directory sends learners to the former enrolment URL, while the current NHS page contains the enrolment route.
queue.evidence: The NHS student page links to the college enrolment form and lists non-digital ways to enrol.

queue.name: Learn Ealing
queue.reason: The empty phone field omits the council’s published Learn Ealing enquiry number.
queue.evidence: The council gives this number in the contact section of its adult learning page.

queue.name: Learn Ealing
queue.currentValue: Browse the course listings and enrol using the details for your chosen course.
queue.proposedValue: Use the council’s Learn Ealing link to register online, then attend an information and advice session. You can call Learn Ealing if you need help getting started.
queue.reason: The council gives two enrolment steps, not just a course search.
queue.evidence: The enrolment section directs learners to register online and attend an IAG session. A contact number is provided below it.

queue.name: Ealing Adult Social Care
queue.currentValue: https://www.ealing.gov.uk/info/201073/health_and_adult_social_care
queue.proposedValue: https://www.ealing.gov.uk/info/201082/what_to_expect_from_adult_social_care/2526/contacting_adult_social_care
queue.reason: The listed index requires extra navigation to reach the contact routes.
queue.evidence: The council contact page links directly to the self-referral form and gives the same telephone number.

queue.name: Ealing Adult Social Care
queue.currentValue: Call the adult social care contact centre or use the council website.
queue.proposedValue: Call the council or use its self-referral form. If you are contacting the council for someone else, make sure they know first; there is a separate form for representatives.
queue.reason: The council distinguishes asking for yourself from contacting it for somebody else.
queue.evidence: The council lists the two forms and asks representatives to make the person aware before making contact.
